sections.overview: Bocourt’s terrific skink is a large New Caledonian skink, known today only from small islets near Île des Pins.
sections.identification: It has an elongated body, short limbs, a robust tail and large, curved front teeth; it is the largest skink in New Caledonia.
sections.habitat: It is associated with low coastal forest on offshore islets.
sections.diet: A 2022 study identified a land crab in its diet and found its bite force sufficient to crack hard crab shells.
sections.behavior: Field observations are scarce; the species is thought to be mainly terrestrial, although individuals have also been seen climbing trunks.
sections.reproduction: Its breeding biology and clutch size remain unknown.
sections.ecology: It is one of two New Caledonian species in Phoboscincus; the other, P. garnieri, is much more widespread and has smoother scales.
sections.conservation: A 2017 New Caledonian Red List assessment classed it as Critically Endangered, citing its tiny known range and threats such as habitat damage and introduced predators.
